parameters.question: The analysis was conducted on a dataset containing 1,901 cells and 36,601 genes, presumably from a non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) context given the file name. After quality control and preprocessing, 96.4% of cells and 71.2% of genes were retained, indicating a high-quality dataset with minimal noise. The UMAP embedding resulted in 15 distinct clusters, with the largest three containing 298, 258, and 220 cells respectively. These clusters should guide the selection of marker genes, with a focus on those that can distinguish between these major cell populations. cell types emphasis certain cell types

CD4+ T cells.rationale: CD4 is a canonical marker for CD4+ T cells. IL2, IFNG, and TNF are cytokines commonly produced by this cell type. CD8A and CD19 are markers for CD8+ T cells and B cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.

CD8+ T cells.rationale: CD8A is a canonical marker for CD8+ T cells. GZMB, PRF1, and IFNG are molecules associated with the cytotoxic function of this cell type. CD4 and CD19 are markers for CD4+ T cells and B cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.

Regulatory T cells.rationale: FOXP3 is a canonical marker for regulatory T cells. CTLA4, IL2RA, and TGFBR1 are molecules associated with the suppressive function of this cell type. CD8A and CD19 are markers for CD8+ T cells and B cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.

B cells.rationale: CD19, CD79A, and MS4A1 are canonical markers for B cells. IGHD is a marker for the B cell receptor. CD3E and CD8A are markers for T cells, which are distinct immune cell types.

Plasma cells.rationale: CD138 and XBP1 are canonical markers for plasma cells. IGHG1 and IGHA1 are markers for the secreted antibodies. CD19 and CD3E are markers for B cells and T cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.

NK cells.rationale: NCAM1 and KLRD1 are canonical markers for NK cells. GZMB and PRF1 are molecules associated with the cytotoxic function of this cell type. CD3E and CD19 are markers for T cells and B cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.

Monocytes/macrophages.rationale: CD68, CD14, and CD163 are canonical markers for monocytes/macrophages. CSF1R is a receptor for a growth factor (CSF1) important for this cell type. CD3E and CD19 are markers for T cells and B cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.

Dendritic cells.rationale: CD11C and CD209 are canonical markers for dendritic cells. HLA-DRA and CCR7 are associated with the antigen-presenting function of this cell type. CD3E and CD19 are markers for T cells and B cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.

Endothelial cells.rationale: PECAM1, CDH5, VEGFR2, and VWF are canonical markers for endothelial cells. CD45 and EPCAM are markers for hematopoietic and epithelial cells respectively, which are distinct cell types.

Fibroblasts / CAFs.rationale: ACTA2, COL1A1, FAP, and PDGFRB are canonical markers for fibroblasts. CD45 and EPCAM are markers for hematopoietic and epithelial cells respectively, which are distinct cell types.

Pericytes.rationale: PDGFRB, RGS5, NG2, and CD146 are canonical markers for pericytes. CD45 and EPCAM are markers for hematopoietic and epithelial cells respectively, which are distinct cell types.

Mast cells.rationale: KIT and FCER1A are canonical markers for mast cells. CPA3 and TPSAB1 are associated with the granules of this cell type. CD3E and CD19 are markers for T cells and B cells respectively, which are distinct immune cell types.
